name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or system to initially access a network.
detection: Monitor application logs for abnormal behavior. Use web application firewalls and IDS signatures.

name: External Remote Services
description: Adversaries may leverage external-facing remote services to initially access a network. VPNs, Citrix, RDP, etc.
detection: Monitor for unusual login times, geolocations, and failed authentication attempts on remote services.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to gain access.
detection: Monitor for unusual account activity, impossible travel, and credential use outside normal patterns.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands and scripts.
detection: Monitor process creation events for unusual scripting engine invocations (PowerShell, bash, Python).

name: PowerShell
description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.
detection: Enable PowerShell script block logging and module logging. Monitor for encoded commands.

name: Exploitation for Client Execution
description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications to execute code.
detection: Monitor for abnormal process behavior from client applications and unexpected child processes.

name: Scheduled Task/Job
description: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling to execute malicious code at system startup or on a scheduled basis.
detection: Monitor for new scheduled tasks or cron jobs, especially those running from unusual paths.

name: Create Account
description: Adversaries may create an account to maintain access to victim systems.
detection: Monitor for new account creation events, especially those with elevated privileges.

name: Web Shell
description: Adversaries may backdoor web servers with web shells to establish persistent access.
detection: Monitor web directories for new or modified files. Detect unusual web server child processes.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities to escalate privileges.
detection: Monitor for unusual privilege changes and exploitation indicators in system logs.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevated privileges.
detection: Monitor for UAC bypass attempts, sudo abuse, and setuid/setgid changes.

name: Process Injection
description: Adversaries may inject code into processes to evade defenses and elevate privileges.
detection: Monitor for unusual process memory modifications and cross-process API calls.

name: Indicator Removal
description: Adversaries may delete or modify artifacts to remove evidence of their presence.
detection: Monitor for log clearing events, file deletion in sensitive directories, and timestomping.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries may dump credentials to obtain account login information.
detection: Monitor for LSASS access, SAM database access, and credential dumping tool signatures.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt access to accounts.
detection: Monitor for multiple failed login attempts and account lockouts.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries may use valid accounts to log into remote services for lateral movement.
detection: Monitor for unusual remote login patterns, especially between workstations.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Adversaries may use RDP to move laterally within a network.
detection: Monitor RDP connection logs for unusual source/destination pairs and times.

name: Lateral Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries may transfer tools between systems within a compromised network.
detection: Monitor for file transfers between internal systems using SMB, WinRM, or other protocols.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.
detection: Monitor for unusual data volumes leaving the network over known C2 channels.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability (ransomware).
detection: Monitor for mass file encryption events, unusual file extension changes, and ransom note creation.

name: Service Stop
description: Adversaries may stop or disable services on a system to render those services unavailable.
detection: Monitor for unexpected service stop events, especially security and backup services.

name: Network Denial of Service
description: Adversaries may perform network DoS attacks to degrade or block availability.
detection: Monitor network traffic for volumetric anomalies and unusual traffic patterns.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries may communicate using OSI application layer protocols to avoid detection.
detection: Monitor for unusual HTTP/HTTPS traffic patterns, DNS tunneling, and beaconing behavior.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries may transfer tools or files from an external system into a compromised environment.
detection: Monitor for file downloads from unusual external sources and known malware hosting sites.

name: Active Scanning
description: Adversaries may execute active reconnaissance scans to gather information for targeting.
detection: Monitor for port scanning activity and vulnerability scanning patterns from external IPs.
